hook: For the first time in history, the Pacific Ocean hit 30 degrees Celsius.

sections.voiceover: For the first time in history, the Pacific Ocean hit 30 degrees Celsius.
sections.visual_cue: Satellite view of the Pacific Ocean with heat map overlay.
b_roll: Global satellite map showing the Pacific region.

sections.voiceover: On October 18, 2026, researchers monitoring the central and equatorial Pacific recorded this unprecedented temperature. How did these waters reach 86 degrees Fahrenheit?
sections.visual_cue: Graph showing rising sea surface temperatures.
sections.sfx_cue: Soft, ticking sound of a clock.

sections.voiceover: This surge is fueling extreme weather patterns globally, ahead of the expected December peak.
sections.visual_cue: Animated map showing weather system movement.

sections.voiceover: Meteorologists confirmed that central tropical Pacific temperatures exceeded 30 degrees Celsius for the first time. The ocean heat remains at record levels across the equatorial region.
sections.visual_cue: Close up of ocean water surface.

sections.voiceover: Average temperatures in the central Pacific now exceed 30 degrees Celsius.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of the Pacific Ocean horizon.
